name: anchor-strips-pid
description: An anchor tracker (utm_source) co-occurs with the ambiguous param `pid`. Contextual rule fires: pid stripped.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — bounded scoping fires when an anchor is present.

name: no-anchor-preserves-pid
description: Standalone `pid` on a non-affiliate host with NO anchor tracker. Functional URL — Contextual rule MUST NOT fire.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — without an anchor, ambiguous params are functional and MUST be preserved.

name: anchor-strips-multiple-pairs
description: Three ambiguous pairs co-occur with a click-id anchor. All three are stripped in one pass.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — every PARAM_PAIRS entry present in the URL is added to removedParams when an anchor co-occurs.

name: anchor-coexists-with-creator-referral
description: Amazon affiliate link with both a creator referral (tag) and an anchor + an ambiguous pair. The referral is preserved (Basic), the pair is stripped (Contextual). The two layers compose.
citation: SPEC §4.4 — Contextual extension composes with the Basic algorithm; affiliate-precedence still wins for creator-referral params.

name: anchor-uppercase-matched-case-insensitively
description: Anchor name in upper case (GCLID). Matching MUST be case-insensitive per §3.2 step 6.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 paragraph: 'Matching of anchor names and pair names MUST be case-insensitive.'

name: pair-uppercase-matched-case-insensitively
description: Pair name in upper case (PID). Matching MUST be case-insensitive; the original casing is preserved in the output.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — case-insensitive matching, original casing preserved.

name: anchor-without-any-pair-stays-defer
description: An anchor is present but the URL carries no ambiguous pair. Nothing for the Contextual extension to strip — algorithm defers.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — anchor presence is necessary but not sufficient; a pair must also be present to strip.

name: anchor-and-empty-value-pair-still-strips
description: Pair value is empty. The Contextual rule fires on KEY presence alone — empty value does not exempt the param.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — rule fires on the (anchor present, pair key present) tuple. Value emptiness is irrelevant for stripping decisions.

name: duplicate-pair-is-deduped
description: Same pair appears twice in the URL. The Contextual rule emits a single entry in removedParams (de-duped on lowercased name).
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — implementations MUST emit at most one removedParams entry per unique lowercased pair name.

name: mailchimp-anchor-strips-pair
description: Exercises the mc_eid Mailchimp anchor family. Behavior mirrors gclid and the others.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — anchor list normatively includes mc_eid and mc_cid.

name: utm-medium-anchor-strips-pair
description: Exercises utm_medium as the anchor (not utm_source). Any UTM core entry MUST trigger the rule.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 6 — utm_source, utm_medium, and utm_campaign are all anchors.

name: network-redirect-host-bypasses-contextual
description: Host is a network-redirect program (Awin). Algorithm short-circuits with decision=network-redirect; Contextual rule MUST NOT add strips. Different action class.
citation: SPEC §3.2 step 5 takes precedence over step 6. Implementations resolve the redirect at a different layer; param-level strips don't apply.
